security_audit.summary: The 50 command-execution alerts and 11 reconnaissance alerts are false positives caused by Markdown tool names and Discord reference rows. The external Rube MCP endpoint is a real low-severity network dependency, while authorized messaging and administration workflows create contextual medium-severity risks.

remediation.suggestion: Document what Discord data and actions Rube MCP can access before users approve an OAuth or bot connection.
Require explicit confirmation before role changes, member updates, webhook changes, reaction deletion, or other broad server actions.
Preview content and confirm recipients before sending direct messages, channel posts, or webhook messages.

content.user_title: Automate Discord Workflows with Rube MCP
content.value_statement: Discord automation requires coordinated tool calls, permissions, and identifiers. This skill guides safe Rube MCP workflows for messages, roles, webhooks, and reactions.
actual_capabilities: Guides assistants to search Rube MCP for current Discord and Discordbot tool schemas.
Helps send channel messages and direct messages after channel or recipient identifiers are known.
Documents role creation, role assignment, role deletion, and member update workflows.
Supports webhook listing, creation, execution, and update workflows through Discordbot tools.
Covers reaction listing and removal workflows with required message and emoji identifiers.
Explains Discord snowflake identifiers, permission bitfields, pagination, and rate-limit handling.
limitations: Requires Rube MCP to be connected and available in the client.
Requires an active Discord or Discordbot connection with valid permissions.
Cannot bypass Discord API permissions, rate limits, or platform policies.
Destructive actions require human review and environment-specific validation.

use_cases.title: Post Server Announcements
use_cases.description: Prepare and send approved announcements to selected Discord channels with verified guild and channel identifiers.

use_cases.title: Maintain Member Roles
use_cases.description: Create, assign, remove, or inspect roles while checking hierarchy and permission limits before each action.

use_cases.title: Connect External Alerts
use_cases.description: Create and execute webhooks for approved integrations that publish operational updates into Discord channels.

prompt_templates.title: Send a Channel Message
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner workflow for one approved message.
prompt_templates.prompt: Send an approved message to a Discord channel. Search Rube MCP for current message tools first. Ask for missing guild or channel identifiers.

prompt_templates.title: Create and Assign a Role
prompt_templates.scenario: Intermediate workflow for member access changes.
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a Discord role and assign it to selected members. Confirm the guild, role name, permissions, member identifiers, and bot hierarchy before execution.

prompt_templates.title: Set Up a Webhook Alert
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a webhook for an approved alert channel. Search for current schemas, confirm the channel and webhook name, then prepare a test message.

prompt_templates.title: Audit a Discord Workflow Plan
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced workflow for controlled multi-step automation.
prompt_templates.prompt: Plan a Discord workflow for messages, roles, and reactions. List each tool call, required identifier, permission check, confirmation point, and rollback option.

output_examples.input: Send a launch announcement to our community updates channel.
output_examples.output: The assistant identifies the guild and channel, previews the announcement, confirms permissions, and sends the message after approval.

output_examples.input: Give three members the event volunteer role.
output_examples.output: The assistant confirms the guild, member identifiers, target role, and hierarchy, then applies the assignments and reports the result.

output_examples.input: Create a webhook for deployment alerts.
output_examples.output: The assistant confirms the target channel, creates the webhook with an approved name, sends a test alert, and protects the token.

best_practices: Search Rube MCP for current tool schemas before choosing a Discord or Discordbot tool.
Confirm guild, channel, user, role, message, and webhook identifiers before executing actions.
Preview outbound messages and require approval for direct messages, webhooks, role changes, and deletions.
anti_patterns: Do not send bulk direct messages or announcements without explicit recipient and content approval.
Do not use administrator permissions when a narrower Discord permission is sufficient.
Do not store or expose webhook tokens, authorization links, or Discord identifiers in shared outputs.

faq.question: Does this skill include executable code?
faq.answer: No. It is a documentation skill that guides Rube MCP tool selection and Discord workflow sequencing.

faq.question: What must be connected before using it?
faq.answer: Rube MCP must be available, and Discord or Discordbot must have an active authorized connection.

faq.question: Can it send messages automatically?
faq.answer: It can guide message sending through Discordbot tools, but users should approve recipients and content first.

faq.question: Can it manage Discord roles?
faq.answer: Yes. It documents role creation, assignment, deletion, and member updates when the bot has permission.

faq.question: How does it handle changing tool schemas?
faq.answer: It instructs the assistant to call RUBE_SEARCH_TOOLS first so current schemas are used.

faq.question: What are the main safety concerns?
faq.answer: The main concerns are third-party authorization, privileged Discord actions, webhook tokens, and unwanted messages.
